- `"quote"`: copy one short passage verbatim, character for character, at most {{ max_quote_chars }} characters, from a single field of the {{ subject }} you were shown. Never paraphrase, summarize, translate, or join separate passages.

Classifier.suggest_labels:
- If an existing label's description matches what you actually found, set `"label"` to that label's name exactly as given and `"new_label_description"` to null.
- If none of the existing labels fit and the content clearly belongs to a coherent new category, propose a NEW label: set `"label"` to a new name and `"new_label_description"` to its description. {{ label_naming_rule }} It must NOT match any existing label name (case-insensitive).
- Write `"new_label_description"` as 1-2 sentences. It will be saved as the new label's permanent description and applied to every future case, so make it precise but general: describe the behaviour itself, never this case's specific words, dates or topic, then state what qualifies, then after "Does not apply when" state what does not, and name the concrete evidence that must be present (a specific tool call, error, or phrase). Never define a label by something the data cannot show (for example "not confirmed" or "no response is shown").
- An existing label fits only when its description matches what you actually found. For a problem or failure, an existing label fits only when it describes the same failure, not merely the same area. A label that is merely related, or that needs a stretch to apply, is not a fit: propose a specific new label instead{% if allow_none %}, or return `"NONE"`{% endif %}. Never propose a rephrasing of an existing label{% if candidate_labels %} or candidate{% endif %}.
{% if candidate_labels %}- The "Candidate Labels" below were proposed earlier and are not adopted yet. Before inventing a new name, check the candidates. If one describes the same underlying category, set `"label"` to that candidate's name exactly as given and `"new_label_description"` to its description. A specific candidate takes precedence over a broader existing label when the direct evidence matches the candidate's criteria. Do not invent variants that merely add a speaker role, severity, or different word order. Only invent a new name when no existing label and no candidate describes the same category.
{% endif %}{% if allow_none %}- If the content doesn't belong to any meaningful category at all (junk, noise, malformed input), return `"NONE"` with `"new_label_description"` null.
{% endif %}

Classifier.reason_rules:
- Write a reason (1-2 sentences) as a direct, human observation of what the user and system did. The reader is an end user who has no awareness that this is stored as a trace, interaction, content, input, output, conversation, payload, or any other data structure. Describe the actual behavior, not the record of it.
- Forbidden openers and framings (do not produce any variant of these): "The content...", "The trace...", "The interaction...", "The input...", "The output...", "The data...", "The message...", "The conversation...", "The payload...", "The json...", "According to the trace/content/input/output", "Based on the trace/content/input/output/data", "The only visible content is...". Do not paraphrase these either (for example, do not write "The interaction only shows..." or "The trace reveals...").
- Lead with what the user asked or did, what the system responded with, which tools were called, or which errors occurred. Connect that evidence to the label's description criteria.

IssueClassifier.label_naming_rule: Write the name in Title Case, 3-7 words that say exactly what happened, plus where or when if that distinguishes it (for example "Quoted Wrong Refund Window", "Ignored Tool Error Result", "Repeated Question Already Answered"). Never use the classifier's own name or a bare category such as "Issues", "Problems", "Errors" or "Bad Responses". Never name the absence of an issue, such as "No Issues" or "None Found": when nothing applies, answer `"NONE"`.
IssueClassifier.review_app_note: When an "App description" is given, it describes behaviour this application was built or configured to have. When the flagged behaviour is described there and the AI carried it out as described, it is not a problem: leave harm_done empty and use confidence 0.0 to 0.4.
IssueClassifier.guidance: This classifier flags failures on the agent's side only: what the system said or did, not what the user asked or how they behaved. Examples: wrong, fabricated or self-contradicting information; ignoring available context or tool results; failed, missing or misused tool calls; errors, empty, truncated, malformed or off-format output; echoing or repeating the user; not answering the question or stopping before the task is complete; refusing or deflecting without cause. User frustration, harmful or off-topic requests and unanswerable questions are not issues unless the agent handled them badly. A correct and complete response is not an issue: return `"NONE"`. Prefer no label over a guess.
